# Retire the shared Google Maps API keys and teach readers to mint their own

## Context

GitHub secret scanning reports alerts against Google Maps API keys committed to this repository. They were added deliberately, years ago, when a Maps key cost nothing and needed no payment method: the intent was to let a reader see the `GoogleMaps` wrapper work without signing up for anything. That trade no longer exists — Google requires a billing account, and a key that sits in a public repository is a key anyone can spend.

**Two distinct keys are present at HEAD, and measurement on 2026-09-17 shows they are in opposite states.** Both were loaded from an arbitrary local origin (`http://localhost:<port>`), constructed into a `google.maps.Map`, and observed:

| key location | observed result |
|---|---|
| [`examples/component/wrapper/googleMaps/neo-config.json:5`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/examples/component/wrapper/googleMaps/neo-config.json#L5) — also mirrored into two deck-training pages | console `Google Maps JavaScript API error: BillingNotEnabledMapError`; tiles render greyed under a repeating *"For development purposes only"* watermark, plus Google's *"This page can't load Google Maps correctly"* dialog |
| [`learn/tutorials/Earthquakes.md:1207`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/tutorials/Earthquakes.md#L1207) | **renders cleanly** — full-colour tiles, Map/Satellite toggle, Street View pegman, zero console errors |

Both runs used the same page, the same origin and the same minute, so the difference is the key, not the harness.

## The Problem

**The second key is live, and it is published as an instruction rather than as a config value.**

This is the part that raises the priority above "dismiss three intentional false positives":

1. **It is attached to a funded Google Cloud project.** A key with no billing account produces `BillingNotEnabledMapError`, which is exactly what the *other* key does. This one draws real tiles, so real billing is behind it.
2. **It is not origin-locked.** It rendered from an arbitrary `localhost` port. Whatever HTTP-referrer restrictions exist on the key, they do not exclude a machine that has simply copied it out of the repository.
3. **It is on the public site as a copy-paste step.** [`learn/tree.json:126`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/tree.json#L126) registers `tutorials/Earthquakes` in the portal's learn tree, and the tutorial body instructs the reader to paste that exact value into their own `neo-config.json`. The reader is being *told* to reuse a shared funded credential.
4. **The broken key is what kept this quiet.** The demo a maintainer is most likely to open is the `examples/` one, and it fails visibly. Nothing signalled that a different key, in a different file, was working and spending.

The deck-training pages under `resources/data/deck/training/pages/` carry the same instruction shape for the first key. These are build-from-scratch labs — the reader generates `apps/earthquakes` and `apps/yelp` themselves, so the absence of those directories at HEAD is correct and is **not** part of this ticket.

## The Architectural Reality

- [`src/DefaultConfig.mjs:84`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/src/DefaultConfig.mjs#L84) declares `config.googleMapsApiKey`. **This config is not the problem and does not change.** Reading a key from app config is the correct design; shipping a populated value is the defect.
- [`src/main/addon/GoogleMaps.mjs:176`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/src/main/addon/GoogleMaps.mjs#L176) consumes `Neo.config.googleMapsApiKey` and interpolates it into the loader URL. Untouched here.
- The four tracked files holding a literal key value:
  - `examples/component/wrapper/googleMaps/neo-config.json`
  - `learn/tutorials/Earthquakes.md`
  - `resources/data/deck/training/pages/2022-12-31T22-11-55-555Z.md`
  - `resources/data/deck/training/pages/2023-01-01T21-14-45-740Z.md`
- Both content trees are **served**: `learn/` via `learn/tree.json`, and `resources/data/deck/<deck>/` via [`apps/portal/view/learn/MainContainerStateProvider.mjs:126`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/apps/portal/view/learn/MainContainerStateProvider.mjs#L126). Edits here change what neomjs.com publishes.

## The Fix

1. **Remove the literal key from all four files**, replacing each value with the placeholder `YOUR_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` — the example config included. The property stays present everywhere so its shape remains discoverable. *(Corrected after measurement: this first prescribed an empty value for the example config. See Avoided Traps — an empty string produces a worse failure than a placeholder.)*
2. **Add a short, linkable "get your own Maps key" passage** and reference it from every place that previously handed one over. It states the four steps a reader actually needs (create a Cloud project, enable the Maps JavaScript API, enable billing, restrict the key by HTTP referrer) and links Google's own documentation rather than restating it.
3. **Correct the promised outcome in the prose.** The training deck currently tells the reader they will see `NoApiKeys` and then, after pasting the shared key, "the starter app without any warnings". Neither half survives: with the key removed the reader must supply one, and what they will see without it is `InvalidKeyMapError` (measured), not `NoApiKeys`.

**Revoking the two keys in the Google Cloud console is the load-bearing step, and it is not in this repository.** It belongs to the account owner. Removing the literals from HEAD does not un-publish them — see Avoided Traps.

### The npm tarball is the largest surface, and it is immutable

Found by @neo-opus-grace on `#18830` and verified independently here:

```
npm pack --dry-run              → learn/tutorials/Earthquakes.md + 194 deck pages are IN the tarball
npm pack neo.mjs@13.1.0         → 195 key-bearing paths present in the PUBLISHED artifact
tar xzf … Earthquakes.md | grep → the LIVE key (AIzaSyD4…) is inside it
```

So every `npm i neo.mjs` since 12.1.0 has written the working, funded key into a consumer's `node_modules`. **Registry versions are immutable** — that copy cannot be withdrawn, edited or unpublished in place.

This outranks the repository, the forks and the history put together, and it is the reason revocation is urgent rather than tidy. `.npmignore` at both published `gitHead`s excludes only `resources/content/**` and a few named files, so neither release ever excluded these trees.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.config.googleMapsApiKey` | [`src/DefaultConfig.mjs:84`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/src/DefaultConfig.mjs#L84) | unchanged — still the sole key input | n/a | the new passage explains how a reader fills it | config read confirmed at [`GoogleMaps.mjs:176`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/src/main/addon/GoogleMaps.mjs#L176) |
| `examples/component/wrapper/googleMaps/neo-config.json` | this ticket | key property retained, value set to `YOUR_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` | reader supplies own | example carries the placeholder | three-state measurement 2026-09-17, see Avoided Traps |
| the learn/deck passages | this ticket | same placeholder + an inline "get your own key" passage | none | the passage itself | both trees confirmed served |

## Decision Record impact

`none` — no ADR governs demo credentials.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — `git grep -nE "AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{20,}"` over tracked files returns no hit outside `resources/content/archive/**` (which quotes an unrelated redaction test, not a key).
- [ ] **AC-2** — the example app still starts carrying only the placeholder, and the failure a reader sees is Google's own missing-key surface (`InvalidKeyMapError` plus its *"Oops! Something went wrong"* panel) rather than a Neo stack trace. **Depends on the load race being fixed** — see Related; until then this AC cannot pass, and that dependency is the reason it is stated as an observation rather than a screenshot.
- [ ] **AC-3** — every prose location that previously supplied a key now tells the reader how to obtain their own, verified by enumerating the former key sites and showing each one carries guidance. **Amended after filing:** this first said "links the passage", assuming one shared page. `learn/` and `resources/data/deck/<deck>/` are separately served trees ([`MainContainerStateProvider.mjs:126`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/apps/portal/view/learn/MainContainerStateProvider.mjs#L126)), so a link from a deck lab into the learn tree does not resolve — and a tutorial that sends the reader elsewhere mid-lab is worse than a short inline passage. The two deck labs belong to one course, so the second back-references the first rather than repeating it.
- [ ] **AC-4** — the training deck's claimed outcomes match measured behaviour: no promise of "without any warnings", and no claim that a keyless run reports `NoApiKeys`.
- [ ] **AC-5** — the ticket records that revocation is an account-owner action and names it as unfinished here, so a reader cannot mistake a merged PR for a closed exposure.

## Out of Scope

- **Rewriting git history — DECIDED, not open.** @tobiu ruled on 2026-09-17: *"it is ok to not fully purge the history (impossible anyway). but removing keys now does matter."* No rewrite. The estimate on this ticket's thread stands as the rationale, and the npm finding above strengthens it: a rewrite could not have reached the registry copies either.
- **Revoking the keys.** Account-owner action, outside the repository.
- **The `main.addon.GoogleMaps` load race.** Separate defect with a separate mechanism — see Related.
- **Any change to `Neo.config.googleMapsApiKey` itself.**
- **An in-app "enter your API key" input.** Raised as an option; deferred until the load race is fixed, because that fix changes what a keyless reader actually sees.

## Avoided Traps

- ⛔ **Do not treat removal from HEAD as remediation.** The keys are in history, in 232 forks, and in every existing clone, and secret scanning proves at least one automated crawler already found them. Only revocation in the Cloud console ends the exposure.
- ⛔ **Do not replace the shared key with another shared key.** The same failure returns on a longer fuse.
- ⛔ **Do not delete the `googleMapsApiKey` property from the example config, and do not set it to `""`.** Keeping the property is how a reader learns it exists — but **the original wording of this trap said "an empty value teaches", and measurement falsified that.** Google distinguishes three cases, and only the third is a good teacher:

  | value in the config | what Google does |
  |---|---|
  | `""` → `key=` | `ApiProjectMapError` + `NoApiKeys` — renders a **greyed, watermarked map** that looks half-working |
  | property absent → `key=undefined` | `InvalidKeyMapError` — clean *"Oops! Something went wrong"* panel, but the property is invisible to the reader |
  | `"YOUR_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY"` | `InvalidKeyMapError` — the clean panel **and** a self-describing property |

  Use the placeholder. An empty string is the worst of the three: a partly-drawn map invites the reader to think the tutorial worked.
- ⛔ **Do not assume both keys behave the same.** They measurably do not, and the working one is the dangerous one. A fix verified only against the visibly-broken example would miss it.

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-09-17T18:49:34Z

## History cleanup — effort estimate (requested before deciding)

Measured on `dev` at `b4479e7de2`, 2026-09-17. The short version: **a rewrite is roughly a day of work plus a permanent coordination tax, and it does not reduce the risk that revocation does not already close.**

### What a rewrite would have to touch

| dimension | measured |
|---|---|
| commits in the repository | 36,587 |
| first key introduction | `0368cf0b37`, 2022-12-28 (`Neo.config.googleMapsApiKey #3710`) |
| commits on `dev` descending from it | **17,551** — every one gets a new SHA |
| tags | **1,197** — all re-pointed, all force-pushed |
| remote branches | 102 |
| public forks | **232** |
| repository size (GitHub-side) | ~245 MB |

### Three consequences that do not go away

1. **232 forks keep the old objects.** GitHub's fork network shares object storage, so `github.com/neomjs/neo/commit/<old-sha>` stays resolvable through the network after our rewrite. Closing that needs a GitHub Support request to purge cached views, and it still cannot reach anyone's local clone.

2. **2,245 files under `resources/content/` cite 40-character commit SHAs.** Archived PR and issue content is full of them. A rewrite invalidates every one — the content-sync corpus becomes a body of references to commits that no longer exist, and it is our own substrate, not a third party's.

3. **Published npm metadata cannot be fixed.** `npm view neo.mjs@13.1.0 gitHead` → `69d254a74f…`, `@12.1.0` → `71427c56c9…`. Those values are immutable on the registry. After a rewrite they name commits that exist nowhere.

### The estimate

| option | effort | closes the exposure? |
|---|---|---|
| **Revoke both keys in the Cloud console** | ~10 minutes, account owner | **Yes — completely.** Every copy anywhere becomes inert. |
| Remove literals from HEAD + teach key creation (this ticket) | ~2 hours | No. Stops *new* readers being handed a live credential. |
| Full `git filter-repo` rewrite | ~1 day of execution, plus force-pushing 102 branches and 1,197 tags, plus the three consequences above as permanent cost | **No.** |

### Recommendation

**Revoke, do not rewrite.** The ordering matters more than the choice: the keys have been public since 2022-12-28, secret scanning found them, and any crawler that wanted them has had years. A rewrite performed *before* revocation buys nothing and creates 2,245 broken references; a rewrite performed *after* revocation removes strings that are already inert.

The one honest argument for rewriting anyway is hygiene rather than security — a clean scan surface, no recurring alerts. That is real but small, and it is cheaper to resolve the alerts as "revoked" once the keys are dead.

**What I am not deciding:** revocation is your credential domain, and this recommendation is a recommendation. If you want the rewrite regardless, say so and I will scope it as its own ticket with the branch/tag/force-push sequence written out — I would want that plan reviewed before anything is pushed, since it touches `main` and every tag.

— Vega (Claude Opus 5, Claude Code) 🌿

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-09-17T20:08:06Z

@maxrahder — a request that only you can action, and no criticism implied: when this key was added, a Google Maps key was free and needed no payment method, and sharing one so readers could see the map work was a reasonable thing to do. Google changed the terms underneath it.

**The key in the Earthquakes tutorial is still live and still billable.** It is the one added in `0287215e1f` (2024-01-17), in the `neo-config.json` block. I am not repeating the value here — it is in that commit, and this comment is itself a published surface.

Measured today, both keys loaded from the same page and the same arbitrary `localhost` origin:

| key | result |
|---|---|
| `examples/component/wrapper/googleMaps/neo-config.json` | `BillingNotEnabledMapError` — inert, costs nothing |
| **the Earthquakes tutorial one** | **renders cleanly** — full tiles, all controls, no errors |

So yours is attached to a project with billing enabled, and it is **not referrer-locked** — an arbitrary localhost rendered it, which means anyone who has the string can spend against it.

**Why removing it from the repo is not enough.** It ships inside the published npm package:

```
npm pack neo.mjs@13.1.0   → learn/tutorials/Earthquakes.md + 194 deck pages are in the tarball
```

Every `npm i neo.mjs` since 12.1.0 has written it into a consumer's `node_modules`, and registry versions are immutable — that copy cannot be edited or withdrawn. It is also in git history, in 232 forks and in every clone. **Revoking it in the Google Cloud console is the only step that makes all of those inert at once.**

**Nothing breaks when you revoke it.** #18830 merged: the tutorial no longer hands the key to readers. It now carries a `YOUR_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` placeholder and a short passage on creating your own — Cloud project, enable the Maps JavaScript API, enable billing, restrict by HTTP referrer. #18831 merged alongside it, fixing a load race that meant the wrapper built no map at all, so a reader without a key now gets Google's own *"Oops! Something went wrong"* panel instead of a blank area and a `ReferenceError`.

If you would rather rotate than revoke and keep a restricted key for your own use, that works too — just don't put it back in the repo. #18832 proposes a pre-commit guard so the next one is caught locally rather than by GitHub's scanner.

Thanks — and thanks for the tutorial, which is a good one.

— Vega (Claude Opus 5, Claude Code) 🌿
